title: Phenotypic DST and critical concentrations
dek: A critical concentration is a cut-point on an MIC distribution, not a cosmic constant. Borderline alleles are where MGIT S/R becomes an argument rather than a measurement.
story: Phenotypic DST asks whether an isolate grows at a WHO-specified critical concentration (CC) of drug in a specified medium (MGIT, 7H10, 7H11, LJ). It is not the same as a clinical breakpoint derived from PK/PD plus outcome, though TB is slowly moving that way for some drugs (moxifloxacin, bedaquiline).

When the MIC distribution of wild-type and resistant populations overlap — ethambutol historically, some rpoB borderline alleles, some Rv0678 modest shifts — a single CC is a coin flip dressed as a column. MIC plus a catalogue grade is more honest.
PZA DST is pH-fragile. Pyrazinamide CCs assume acidified media; a failed pH control is a false-R factory. Never “confirm” a messy PZA MGIT by shouting at pncA; use both.
deep: Epidemiological cut-off (ECOFF) marks the upper edge of the apparent wild-type MIC distribution. Clinical breakpoints add PK/PD. TB CCs have historically mixed those ideas.
CRyPTIC and WHO CC revisions exist because 20-year-old numbers were wrong for some drugs. Your SOP year matters in a methods section.
Direct DST from smear-positive sputum trades speed for contamination and mix. Indirect DST from a MGIT subculture can lose a minority.
For BDQ and LZD, MIC methods are preferred over a single poorly powered CC if you have them. Catalogue + MIC is the adult conversation.

visual.caption: Wild-type and resistant MIC densities. A CC (dashed, schematic at 0.5 on this axis) cleanly splits some drugs (RIF S450L) and slices through others (borderline rpoB, EMB).

example.title: rpoB H445D, MGIT RIF-S, rifabutin pending
example.setup: Borderline-ish RRDR allele. MGIT RIF at CC reports S. Ultra called RIF-R. MIC is 1 dilution above modal WT.

steps.title: Do not call the MGIT the referee of nature
steps.body: This is the overlap zone the density plate is about.

steps.title: Catalogue plus MIC
steps.body: WHO grades many 445 alleles as associated with RIF-R, sometimes with rifabutin spared. Report the allele and the MIC.

steps.title: Clinically this is not 2HRZE on autopilot
steps.body: RR algorithms exist for disputed mutations. Local expert/NTP SOP, not a tweet.

example.takeaway: A CC is a policy cut on a distribution.

choices: The Cmax in plasma for every patient
A specified concentration used to dichotomise growth as S/R in a specified method
Always identical to the ECOFF and to the PK/PD breakpoint
check.answer: A specified concentration used to dichotomise growth as S/R in a specified method
check.why: Method-dependent cut-point, not a cosmic MIC.

check.prompt: If WT MIC 95th percentile is 0.25 and a borderline mutant MIC sits at 0.5, a CC of 0.5 will:
choices: Always call the mutant R with infinite likelihood
Slice near the overlap, so S/R labels become unstable across labs and methods
check.answer: Slice near the overlap, so S/R labels become unstable across labs and methods
check.why: That is why MIC and catalogue grades exist.

check.prompt: On the MIC density plate, which curve is the reason a single CC can look arbitrary?
check.why: The middle curve overlaps the cut.

whyWrong.wild-type only: Cleanly left if the CC is well placed.
whyWrong.none of the curves: The borderline curve is the lesson.

check.figureHint: Three curves: WT, high-level R, borderline.
